  Translator's Summary — Section 9
  
    Winter 5565: Rabbainu commands the re-transcription of all Torah teachings from scattered notebooks into one ordered volume, fit for binding. Rabbi Naftali reads aloud word by word; Reb Nussun writes. Process takes about a quarter of a year — through Pesach to near Shavuos.
    Strict secrecy: Despite the transcription work, Rabbainu does not reveal any intent to print. Torah strictly guarded from all outsiders. Notebooks kept hidden.
    A peculiar obstacle: Between Pesach and Shavuos, Reb Nussun visits Rabbainu several times. Rabbainu feigns displeasure at the frequency of visits — creating an internal obstacle far heavier than material ones. The disciples no longer worry about money or family pressure — only: "will he be displeased that we came so soon?" Yet love overcomes every time.
    After Shavuos: Reb Nussun is in spiritual distress, longs desperately to come to Rabbainu, but cannot face another "so soon" arrival. G-d provides an aytzah: travel to Breslov to have the book bound (which Rabbainu himself commanded must be done in Breslov, not Nemirov, to avoid the many opponents there). This becomes the pretext for coming.
    Friday morning arrival: Reb Nussun arrives and hides at the bookbinder, too ashamed to face Rabbainu. Rabbainu spots him passing by, queries him about why he came. When Reb Nussun answers "to bind the book," Rabbainu asks pointedly: "And for this you needed to come deliberately?" — Reb Nussun is struck dumb with awe.
    The "left pushes away, right draws close": Rabbainu sends a messenger to fetch Reb Nussun from the bookbinder (sending the messenger to guard the books in his place). Reb Nussun runs. Rabbainu lies on his bed in his small room and speaks with him at great length with extraordinary warmth — consoling, gladdening, and strengthening him with words sweeter than honey.
    Revelation of the Ten Psalms (Tikun HaKlali): That same day, before Reb Nussun's arrival, Rabbainu had said the Torah on the remedy for a nocturnal fall (Likutay Moharan §205). Reb Nussun had missed it. His son-in-law Rabbi Yitzchok partially explains it; Rabbainu himself then clarifies and Reb Nussun writes it immediately. At this stage, which specific psalms are not yet revealed — only that ten psalms corresponding to the ten kinds of song are to be said. The specific chapters are revealed only years later (Likutay Tinyanna §92).
    All Friday: Rabbainu unusually delays his Friday bathhouse visit until late afternoon. He speaks the famous words: "How difficult it is to be renowned, to guide the world!" Then: "You think the binding of this book counts for nothing? — how many worlds depend on it!" Teaches Reb Nussun from afar: nothing in his affairs is trivial.
    An entire week of strengthening: Bookbinder is slow; Reb Nussun stays through the following Thursday. All week Rabbainu speaks to him exclusively of strengthening in joy — using the parable of the sick person who recovers precisely by not giving in to his illness's heaviness.
    Rabbainu shares his suffering: Reveals that he physically feels in his heart every groan of his ill grandchild. Would gladly take the illness upon himself. This is the "ways of G-d that cannot be understood" — like the Ari who was compelled by Reb Chaim Vital to reveal a secret, yet whose son then died as a consequence. Rabbainu: all his sufferings come from his occupation with drawing us close — his intent is purely for Heaven, G-d wills it — yet he is punished for it. This cannot be comprehended.
    He feels every Jew's pain: Even when strangers come to ask him to pray for a sick infant — he feels that infant's every groan exactly as he feels his own grandchild's. And when any person becomes estranged from the circle — the same anguish.
    Thursday: Book bound. Reb Nussun brings it before Rabbainu. Rabbainu says: "You are still not in joy. In time to come, you will know my greatness." (Yiddish: Amol vesstu vissen mein groiskait.) He then hints at his awesome burned book.
  

  Translator's Note — On Completeness: This rendering is the complete and unabridged translation of the Preface and Sections 1 through 9 of Yimay Moharnat, Part One. Every sentence of the Hebrew has been rendered without condensation, omission, or paraphrase. Parenthetical clarifications added by the translator appear in [square brackets]. Yiddish phrases are given in transliteration followed by their meaning. All transliterations follow Ashkenazic pronunciation throughout, with tzairai rendered "ai" and the letter Tuv without a dagesh rendered "s."
  

  Sections 10 onwards continue the narrative through the years 5566–5570, covering Reb Nussun's periods in Mohilov, the journeys to Zaslov and Lemberg, the printing of Likutay Moharan, the passing of Rabbainu's first wife, and much more — to be translated in full in subsequent installments, b'ezras Hashem Yisborach.
